title: Inside Sabyasachi's New York Diwali Party: Peacock Centrepiece, Chaat Counter, Kaling in Gold
excerpt: At his Madison Avenue flagship, Sabyasachi Mukherjee staged Diwali with a peacock adapted from a 1920s Banarasi sari, a regional-Indian menu by chef Tushar Ghei, and guests including Mindy Kaling and Ayesha Curry.
body:
• Sabyasachi Mukherjee hosted a Diwali party at his New York flagship on Madison Avenue, with a hand-painted peacock centrepiece adapted from a 1920s Banarasi sari, strawberry pyramids and a live chaat counter.
  • Guests included Mindy Kaling, Jessel Taank and Ayesha Curry; the menu paired regional Indian dishes by chef Tushar Ghei with a Mumbai-style sandwich and chaat station.
  • The decor was built by the same artisans and craftspeople the label works with in India, flown-in craftsmanship that has become a signature of Sabyasachi's US retail push.
  • The party is part of the label's stateside expansion, which includes a Houston store and an upcoming Los Angeles flagship.

Sabyasachi Mukherjee turned his New York flagship into a Diwali set piece this week, hosting a party at 844 Madison Avenue where a hand-painted peacock centrepiece, pyramids of strawberries and a working chaat counter made the case that the Indian luxury label's American expansion will be staged at full spectacle.

The centrepiece, described by Hindustan Times and photographed by Vogue, adapted a peacock motif from a 1920s Banarasi sari in the brand's archives, hand-painted in fading golds, greens and blues and set amid pomegranates, grapes, hydrangeas and monstera leaves. Tall taper candles, red roses and still-life paintings in gold frames lined a grazing table built from toast, strawberry pyramids and Indian sweets, while tall silver bar counters anchored the room. Mukherjee told Vogue the decor was executed by the same artisans the house works with in India: "We have no set designers. We work with the same artisans and craftspeople that we do in India, and we put the parties together ourselves."

"We have no set designers. We work with the same artisans and craftspeople that we do in India, and we put the parties together ourselves."

— Sabyasachi Mukherjee to Vogue

A menu built as a tour of India

Chef Tushar Ghei's menu ran region to region: a Mumbai sandwich and live chaat counter, slow-cooked Old Delhi butter chicken, saffron biryani with mirchi ka salan and a baked Alaska flambéed tableside. Guests photographed through the evening included Mindy Kaling — who wore a beige-and-gold embroidered Sabyasachi ensemble — Jessel Taank and Ayesha Curry, alongside figures from New York's fashion and media circles.

Why the party is a business story

The evening doubled as retail strategy. Sabyasachi's US footprint has grown from the Madison Avenue flagship to a Houston store, with a Los Angeles flagship in the works, and Diwali has become the label's marquee moment to put Indian craft in front of American fashion's decision-makers on their own calendar. The peacock-from-a-sari centrepiece is the pitch in miniature: archival Indian textile craft, presented at a scale and finish meant to stand comparison with any Western luxury house's holiday installation.

For diaspora shoppers, the label's US stores have changed the bridal and occasion-wear calculation — fittings and trunk shows in New York and Houston instead of a buying trip to Kolkata or Mumbai. Parties like this one are how the brand keeps that audience, and the fashion press that influences it, inside the store.
